'''Jūgosha Shrine''' (十五社神社) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Yamagata, Gifu|en|Yamagata, Gifu|qid=Q773311|lt=Yamagata City}}, Gifu Prefecture. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines}}, it held the Rank of {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917316|qq= 近代社格制度}} and was classified as a {{ill|Kinpei-sha|ja|金幣社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinpeisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q119929592}} under Gifu Prefecture’s unique shrine classification system. It was established in {{ill|Tenchō|en|Tenchō|qid=Q1373138|lt=Tenchō (era)}} 3 (826 CE) by {{ill|Haruhara no Ioe|ja|春原五百枝|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haruhara Ioe|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11513416}}, who constructed the shrine to enshrine the deity known as "Amatsukami Daimyōjin."

The shrine enshrines deities from the {{ill|Kamiyonanayo|en|Kamiyonanayo|qid=Q3275893|lt=Kamiyonanayo}}, the divine lineage of Japan’s emperors, and the tutelary deities of the Genji clan, offering blessings for national security, prosperity of the imperial family, and familial safety.

The shrine was revered by the {{ill|Toki clan|en|Toki clan|qid=Q687635|lt=Toki clan}} during the {{ill|Sengoku Period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q117415390}} as their tutelary deity.

The shrine’s main hall, rebuilt under the orders of {{ill|Tokugawa Tsunayoshi|en|Tokugawa Tsunayoshi|qid=Q313745|lt=Tokugawa Tsunayoshi}}, is designated as a Gifu Prefecture Important Cultural Property. The {{ill|Shakudani Stone|ja|笏谷石|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokudani stone|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11599510}} komainu donated by the Toki clan are recognized as a Yamagata City Important Cultural Property.

== History ==
According to legend, in May of {{ill|Tenchō|en|Tenchō|qid=Q1373138|lt=Tenchō (era)}} 3 (826 CE), amid fierce lightning and hail, the deity {{ill|Ame-no-Tokotachi|ja|天之常立神}} and 17 other deities from the Kamiyonanayo and Chijin-godai descended, instructing the construction of a shrine for national protection before departing. Some theories link the shrine to the "Seishin Myōjin" mentioned in the {{ill|Izumi Province Divine Name Register|ja|国内神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mino no Kuni Shinsen Meishocho|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11420490}}, listed among the 12 shrines in {{ill|Yamagata District, Hiroshima|en|Yamagata District, Hiroshima|qid=Q1155572|lt=Yamagata District, Gifu}}.

During the {{ill|Muromachi period|en|Muromachi period|qid=Q334845|lt=Muromachi period}}, {{ill|Toki Yorinari|en|Toki Yorinari|qid=Q837179|lt=Toki Yorie}} brought the spirit of {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|en|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|qid=Q710098|lt=Iwashimizu Hachimangū}} to the shrine, merging it and renaming it "Jūgosha Daigongen." It became the clan deity of the Toki family. In {{ill|Genroku|en|Genroku|qid=Q1325001|lt=Genroku}} 14 (1701), the main hall was rebuilt. Later, during the {{ill|Culture|en|Culture|qid=Q11042|lt=Bunka}} era (1804–1818), the shrine was renamed "Jūgosha Daijingū."

In {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} 5 (1872), it was renamed to its current name and designated a village shrine. It was promoted to a gōsha in 1944.

== Rituals ==
;Yu-barai (Ritual Purification by Boiling Water)
:This ritual is said to be a remnant of ancient trial-by-boiling-water {{ill|Kuchiyose|en|Kugatachi|qid=Q11581453|lt=Kuga no Utagai}}. A large cauldron is set over a fire, and the {{ill|Ōharae no Kotoba|en|Ōharae no Kotoba|qid=Q11438317|lt=Ōharai Norito}} is recited a thousand times.

== Cultural Properties ==
Gifu Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties:
* Main Hall<ref name="jugoshajinja">{{Cite web|title=Jūgosha Shrine|url=https://www.city.yamagata.gifu.jp/site/yamanavi/1132.html|publisher=Yamagata City|accessdate=2023-12-04}}</ref> - Built in the {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|en|Nagare-zukuri|qid=Q210684|lt=Nagare-zukuri}} style with a hinoki bark roof, reconstructed in Genroku 14 (1701).
Yamagata City Designated Cultural Properties:
* {{ill|Komainu|en|Komainu|qid=Q20155846|lt=Komainu}}<ref name="jugoshajinja"/> - Donated in {{ill|Tenmon|ja|天文|qid=Q21096812}} 9 (1540) by the Toki clan, carved from {{ill|Shakudani Stone|ja|笏谷石|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokudani stone|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11599510}}.
City-Designated Natural Monuments:
* Henmi Cedar<ref name="jugoshajinja"/> - A cedar tree with a circumference of 5.2 meters. Legend states it was planted by {{ill|Henmi Shigekazu|ja|逸見重氏}}.

== Transportation ==
* From the Hā Bus line Ōga route, alight at "Shikokuyama Kaori no Mori Kōen" bus stop, then walk for 15 minutes.

'''Jūgoshajinja''' (十五社神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto}} shrine located in {{ill|Yamagata, Gifu|en|Yamagata, Gifu|qid=Q773311|lt=Yamagata City (Gifu)}}, Gifu Prefecture. It was designated as a former {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917316|qq= 近代社格制度}} under the modern shrine Rank system and holds the unique Gifu Prefectural Rank of Kanpeisha. The shrine was established in Tenchō 3 (826 CE) by Haruhara Ioe, who built the shrine to enshrine the deity {{ill|Ame-no-Tokotachi|ja|天之常立神}}.

The shrine venerates deities connected to the Japanese imperial lineage, from the {{ill|Kamiyonanayo|en|Kamiyonanayo|qid=Q3275893|lt=Kamiyonanayo}} to the first emperor, reflecting divine virtues of national stability, royal prosperity, and familial safety. During the {{ill|Sengoku Period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku Period|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q117415390}}, the shrine was revered as the clan shrine of the {{ill|Toki clan|en|Toki clan|qid=Q687635|lt=Toki clan}}.

Its main hall, reconstructed under the orders of Tokugawa Tsunayoshi, is designated a Gifu Prefectural Important Cultural Property, and the shrine's stone guardian lions, donated by the Toki clan, are designated as cultural assets by Yamagata City.

== History ==
According to tradition, in May of Tenchō 3 (826 CE), a fierce storm accompanied by thunder and hail brought down the deities {{ill|Ame-no-Tokotachi|ja|天之常立神}} and other members of the {{ill|Kamiyonanayo|en|Kamiyonanayo|qid=Q3275893|lt=Kamiyonanayo}} and {{ill|Five Generations of Earth Deities|lt=Five Generations of Earth Deities|lt=Chijin Godai|ja|地神五代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chijin Godai}}. These deities instructed the establishment of a shrine for the nation’s protection before disappearing. It is believed that this shrine corresponds to "Shōshi Myōjin" (正四位下 裁主明神) listed in the {{ill|Mino Province's Shrine Ledger|ja|美濃国神名帳}}.

During the {{ill|Muromachi period|en|Muromachi period|qid=Q334845|lt=Muromachi period}}, the Toki clan, ruling from Ōga Castle, invited the {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|en|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|qid=Q710098|lt=Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine}} deity to the shrine and renamed it "Jūgoshajinja." In {{ill|Genroku|en|Genroku|qid=Q1325001|lt=Genroku}} 14 (1701 CE), the main hall was reconstructed, and in {{ill|Culture|en|Culture|qid=Q11042|lt=Bunka}} 9 (1812 CE), the shrine was renamed "Jūgosha Daijingu" by Prince Iwakura Tomosue. In 1872, it was renamed to its current name and designated as a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917284|qq= 近代社格制度}}, later upgraded to a Gōsha in 1944.

== Rituals ==
; Yubarai (湯祓)
: This ancient purification ritual is a vestige of {{ill|Kuchiyose|en|Kugatachi|qid=Q11581453|lt=Kuchiyose}}, in which boiling water was used for divine oaths. A large cauldron is heated while the {{ill|Ōharae no Kotoba|en|Ōharae no Kotoba|qid=Q11438317|lt=Ōharae Kotoba}} is chanted 1,000 times.
